Master Itinerary

How to read this

  • AnchorFixed, time-critical commitments. Everything else bends around these.
  • Flex menuPick one or split up. Walking/travel times are listed so you can regroup.
  • Meal menuResearched choices with approximate cost, hours and walking time. The default pick is marked.
  • Choose oneA single either/or decision (e.g., Montserrat cable car vs. rack railway).

Dotted-underline names jump to the glossary; the glossary entry links to the official site.

Day 1 · Saturday, Nov. 28

Roman & Medieval Barcelona

2:00 PM MUHBA Plaça del Rei7:00 PM Tapas at Tapeo
9:00 AM

Arrive at BCN

Allow about 60–75 min for passport control and customs.

10:15–10:50
Airport → apartment neighborhoodPrivate transfer/taxi · about 30–40 min. One of the few car rides worth keeping, since all five of you have carry-ons.
11:00 AM–12:00 PM
Meal menu

Casual lunch near the apartment

Default pickEL CAFE DE L'EIXAMPLE↗
Family-run/casual Mediterranean café; €10–20. Relaxed and inexpensive after the flight. To apartment: 5–10 min.
En Diagonal↗
Small neighborhood café/tapas spot, good coffee and well-praised bravas. €. To apartment: 8–12 min. More local, less touristy.
Miss Simona↗
Brunch: eggs, focaccia, salads, pancakes, specialty coffee. €10–20. Opens 9:30 AM. To apartment: 8–10 min. Best if the group wants brunch over Spanish lunch.

Recommendation: keep EL CAFE DE L'EIXAMPLE as the default unless the group wants brunch.

12:00–12:30
Walk to Apartment Lucia & drop luggageCarrer de Sardenya 213 · 5–10 min walk, then about 20 min to drop bags.
12:30–1:00
Apartment → Barri GòticMetro: Sagrada Família → L2 → Passeig de Gràcia → L4 → Jaume I, then a short walk · about 25–30 min door-to-door.
1:00–1:45

Catedral de Barcelona / Barcelona Cathedral + Roman wall remains

Your introduction to medieval Barcelona before going underground into Roman Barcino.

2:00–4:00 PM
Anchor

MUHBA Plaça del Rei / Barcelona History Museum — King’s Square Site

One of the trip’s highest-priority sights. You descend below modern Barcelona and walk through Roman streets, workshops and industrial areas, with later historical layers above, rather than looking at artifacts in cases.

4:00–5:00

Gothic Quarter walk

  • 4:00Plaça Sant Jaume: City Hall and the Catalan government palace.
  • 4:20Carrer del Bisbe / Bishop’s Street: short atmospheric route under the decorative bridge.
  • 4:35El Call / Jewish Quarter: medieval lanes of Barcelona’s historic Jewish district.
  • 4:50Walk toward Santa Maria del Mar.
5:00–6:30 PM
Flex menu

Flex menu

A — Santa Maria del Mar
Best for Gothic architecture and church history. Walk 0–5 min · visit 45–60 min.
B — El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria
More archaeology/history. MUHBA is Roman; this preserves Barcelona around 1700. Walk 5–10 min · visit 45–60 min.
C — Museu Marítim de Barcelona
Ships and naval history in the medieval Royal Shipyards. Walk 20–25 min · visit 60–90 min. Only if someone specifically wants maritime history.
D — Relaxed El Born
Church interior + coffee/hot chocolate/pastry + medieval streets. 2–10 min between stops.
E — Shopping / browsing
Carrer de Montcada and surrounding lanes. You are already there.

Regroup: 6:30 PM near Tapeo.

7:00–8:15 PM
Anchor + Meal menu

Tapas in El Born

Default pick · AnchorTapeo↗
Compact, lively El Born tapas with traditional dishes given a modern touch. Great for sharing lots of plates. 0–5 min from the flex area. Reserve for five.
Bar del Pla↗
Market-driven Catalan tapas, thoughtful but not fussy. €20–30. About 5 min from Tapeo/Santa Maria del Mar.
Taller de Tapas – Argenteria↗
Larger restaurant-style room with a broad menu and easier seating for five. 5–8 min. Best backup if the smaller places are packed.

Good order for the table: bravas, croquetas, tortilla española, pan con tomate, jamón ibérico, padrón peppers, bombas and seafood. Alcohol-free drinks are completely normal here: sparkling water, soft drinks and coffee are easy.

8:15 PM onward
Flex menu

Flex evening

Gothic Quarter at night
Walk the illuminated cathedral/civic core.
Dessert / hot chocolate
Easy low-energy option.
More El Born
Stay out if everyone still has energy.
Head home
Jaume I → L4 → Passeig de Gràcia → L2 → Sagrada Família · about 25–30 min.
Day 2 · Sunday, Nov. 29

Sagrada, Modernisme, Mozart & Compline

9:00 AM Sagrada Família Mass5:00 PM Mozart at the Liceu9:00 PM Compline at St. James
7:30–8:00 AM
Meal menu

Fast breakfast before Mass

Best quality + convenienceBO&MIE Barcelona↗
French bakery steps from Sagrada Família; opens 7:00 AM daily. Coffee, croissants, bread, pastries. From apartment: 10–15 min.
365 Obrador↗
Cheap counter-service bakery/café; opens 6:00 AM. €1–10. Fastest coffee + pastry/sandwich right at Sagrada Família.
Cumin Brunch & Café↗
Hearty eggs/brunch plates, coffee, juice; opens 7:00 AM. €10–20. Only if you can stay on schedule.
Apartment breakfast
Fastest of all: groceries/pastries kept at the apartment. Zero detour and maximum buffer for the 9:00 AM Mass.

For Sunday, favor BO&MIE or apartment breakfast so you are at the basilica early.

8:10–8:25
Walk to Sagrada FamíliaAbout 10–15 min from the apartment.
9:00–10:00 AM
Anchor 1

International Mass at Sagrada Família / Holy Family

Arrive early: admission is free but capacity is limited. After Mass, use 10:00–10:30 for exterior photos.

10:30–10:45
Walk Avinguda de Gaudí → Sant PauAbout 10–15 min.
10:45–11:45

Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau / Saint Paul Art Nouveau Site

Former hospital complex with ornate Modernista pavilions, gardens, tilework and underground passages.

12:00–1:15 PM
Meal menu

Tapas lunch near Sant Pau / Sagrada

Default pickSagradas Tapas↗
Classic tapas on Avinguda de Gaudí; about €20–40, open from 11:00 AM Sunday. Standouts: bravas, croquettes, mussels, calamari, Catalan sausage. From Sant Pau: 5–8 min.
Madre Taberna Moderna↗
Modern Spanish/Mediterranean tapas, more polished. From Sant Pau: 10–12 min toward Sagrada. Good for a nicer sit-down lunch.
La Llesca↗
Catalan restaurant, average €25. Better if some want Catalan mains over a second tapas meal. 10–12 min.

If Sunday is your second dedicated tapas meal, Sagradas Tapas remains the best logistical fit.

1:15–4:15 PM
Flex menu

Flex menu #1

A — Casa Batlló
Another major Gaudí experience. Travel 20–25 min · visit 75–90 min.
B — Casa Milà – La Pedrera
Gaudí rooftop and architecture. Travel 20–25 min · visit 60–90 min.
C — Passeig de Gràcia
Best free architecture choice: Batlló + Pedrera exteriors. ~20 min metro; 10–15 min between buildings.
D — Picasso Museum
Best for art. Travel 25–30 min · visit 60–90 min. Then 15–20 min to the Liceu.
E — Shopping
Best around Passeig de Gràcia. Travel ~20 min.
F — Café / dessert / people-watching
Low effort; stay near Sagrada or move toward Passeig de Gràcia.
G — Apartment / rest
Walk back 10–15 min. Apartment → Liceu later: 25–30 min by metro.

Regroup: 4:30 PM at the Liceu.

5:00 PM
Anchor 2

Mozart at the Gran Teatre del Liceu / Liceu Grand Theatre

La clemenza di Tito. Stay for the first half and leave at intermission, expected roughly 6:15–6:30 PM.

6:30–7:00
Walk toward the Gothic Quarter / dinner area
7:00–8:00 PM
Meal menu

Fast Gothic Quarter dinner before St. James

Best logistical fitRestaurant Gòtic↗
Catalan/Spanish with tapas and rice dishes. Open Sunday. From Liceu: 7–10 min; a few minutes to St. James. Great for a strict one-hour dinner.
Braseria Ferran↗
Casual Mediterranean grill and rice restaurant, broad menu, good value. From Liceu: 8–10 min.
Casa Pince↗
Central Mediterranean/Catalan with an easy menu for a mixed group. From Liceu: 5–7 min.

You need to be at St. James by 8:45. Reserve for 7:00 and tell the restaurant you must leave by 8:00.

8:00–8:45 PM

B — Plaça Sant Jaume

9:00 PM
Anchor 3

Planned Compline at Església de Sant Jaume / Saint James Church

Afterward, return to the apartment by public transit, roughly 25–30 min.

Verification note: this is the service you want to attend, but the current official Saint James page describes the building as a church (not a cathedral) and does not presently list a 9:00 PM Sunday Compline. Keep it as the planned anchor, but re-verify the Nov. 29 service before the trip.

FGC R5 toward Montserrat
Mountain ascent
Choose one

Choose one

A — Aeri de Montserrat (cable car)
Best for dramatic views and speed. Get off at Montserrat-Aeri. Final ride ~5 min; standing cabin can feel crowded.
B — Cremallera de Montserrat (rack railway)
Best for comfort and seating. Stay on R5 to Monistrol de Montserrat and transfer to the rack railway.
~10:00–11:45

Monestir de Montserrat / Montserrat Monastery + basilica + Black Madonna

11:45 AM–12:30 PM
Meal menu

Montserrat lunch before the choir

Default pickLa Cafeteria
Official hours 8:45 AM–6:30 PM Mon–Fri. Fastest reliable pre-choir choice: sandwiches, snacks, cafeteria-style food. Minimal walking.
Bar Mirador dels Apòstols
Official hours 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. Quick food with mountain views.
Bar de la Plaça
Open from 8:45 AM Mon–Thu. Simple, fast option in the main sanctuary area.
Buffet Montserrat — AFTER choir only
Opens 12:15 PM, too risky before the choir. If chosen, see the choir first, then eat ~1:15–2:00 PM and shorten the mountain flex block. Promoted as quick and good value.
Hostal Abat Cisneros — AFTER choir only
Lunch hours 1:00–3:00 PM. A more traditional sit-down meal, but it will use most of the afternoon flex period.

Important: the old 11:45–12:35 lunch block did not fit the official buffet/restaurant hours. To protect the 1:00 PM choir, use La Cafeteria, Bar Mirador or Bar de la Plaça.

12:35

Escolania de Montserrat / Montserrat Boys’ Choir

Meal menu

Day 4 · Tuesday, Dec. 1

Santa Florentina + Carcassonne Road Trip

11:00 AM Santa Florentina Castle~3:00 PM Count’s Castle + Ramparts~6:20 PM Jeff de Bruges~7:30 PM Lower-town French dinner
Rental-car plan: reserve a car that explicitly permits cross-border driving from Spain into France. Ideally pick it up Monday evening or very early Tuesday so rental paperwork does not consume the morning.
7:15–8:00 AM
Meal menu

Breakfast + road-food setup

Best strategyBreakfast at apartment + pack snacks
Eat quickly and bring water, fruit and snacks. Protects the Santa Florentina appointment and keeps the road day flexible.
365 Obrador↗
Opens 6:00 AM. Coffee/pastry plus inexpensive sandwiches or savory bakery items for the car.
BO&MIE↗
Opens 7:00 AM. Better pastries and sandwiches; slightly less grab-and-run.
~8:30 AM
Leave BarcelonaRental car · Barcelona → Canet de Mar about 45–60 min.
~9:30–10:45

Canet de Mar buffer

Park, coffee/restroom, walk toward the castle. On Tuesdays the castle advises parking on nearby streets before the dirt access road.

9:30–10:40 AM
Meal menu

Canet de Mar food / takeaway

Best road-food pickCafeteria Flama del Canigó↗
Local café known for entrepans de coca (Catalan sandwiches), tortillas and breakfast plates. Opens 7:00 AM Tuesday. Buy sandwiches to take with you.
Bruma Coffee & Bakery↗
Cozy bakery/café; opens 8:00 AM. Excellent coffee and pastries; best for breakfast/snacks.
El Gra↗
Everyday local café: coffee, croissants, empanadas, bocadillos, salads. Opens 7:00 AM. Quick takeaway fallback.

Recommendation: buy sandwiches in Canet before the castle; eat them during a short motorway rest stop after the 12:00 departure.

11:00 AM–12:00 PM
Anchor 1

Castell de Santa Florentina / Santa Florentina Castle

Medieval-origin castle extensively redesigned during the Catalan Modernista period — a very different architectural experience from Carcassonne.

12:00–~2:45 PM
Drive to CarcassonneAbout 2½ hours. Eat the Canet sandwiches at a short motorway rest stop; this protects the ticketed castle before it closes.

The main ticketed attraction inside the much larger walled city. Go straight here on arrival because the château/ramparts have the hard winter closing time.

Anchor + Meal menu

French dinner in Bastide Saint-Louis

Traditional pickAu lard et au cochon↗
Small traditional French restaurant near Place Carnot; strong for cassoulet and generous regional cooking. Tuesday dinner 7:00–9:00 PM. A few min from Place Carnot.
Le-Bis-Troquet↗

Glossary of Sites

Click a site name to open its official page. Links in the itinerary above jump here.

Carrer del Bisbe / Bishop’s Street↗

Narrow historic street beside Barcelona Cathedral, famous for the ornate neo-Gothic bridge overhead.
Why it matters: A short visual stop linking Saint James Square, the Cathedral area and the old Jewish Quarter.

Plaça Sant Jaume / Saint James Square↗

Barcelona’s historic civic square, with City Hall and the Palau de la Generalitat.
Why it matters: Connects ancient civic Barcelona with the city’s modern political center.

El Call / Jewish Quarter↗

Medieval Jewish district made up of narrow lanes within the Gothic Quarter.
Why it matters: Adds a different layer of medieval Barcelona beyond churches and royal buildings.

Catedral de Barcelona / Barcelona Cathedral↗

Main Gothic cathedral of Barcelona, formally the Cathedral of the Holy Cross and Saint Eulalia.
Why it matters: Major medieval church stop and the lead-in to the Roman archaeology at MUHBA.

MUHBA Plaça del Rei / Barcelona History Museum — King’s Square Site↗

History-museum complex with extensive underground Roman remains beneath King’s Square.
Why it matters: One of your top priorities; this is where you actually walk through ancient Roman Barcelona.

Barri Gòtic / Gothic Quarter↗

Barcelona’s old-city district of Roman remains, medieval streets, churches and civic buildings.
Why it matters: The main historical setting for Saturday.

Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar / Basilica of Saint Mary of the Sea↗

Major 14th-century Catalan Gothic basilica tied to the merchant and maritime quarter.
Why it matters: Shows the merchant/seafaring side of medieval Barcelona, distinct from the Cathedral.

El Born / Born District↗

Historic neighborhood east of the Gothic Quarter, associated with merchants, markets and crafts.
Why it matters: Where your Saturday flex period and tapas dinner are centered.

El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria / Born Centre for Culture and Memory↗

Former market building covering preserved streets and buildings from Barcelona around 1700.
Why it matters: Optional later-history archaeology that complements rather than duplicates MUHBA.

Museu Marítim de Barcelona / Barcelona Maritime Museum↗

Maritime museum housed in Barcelona’s historic Royal Shipyards.
Why it matters: Saturday flex choice for anyone particularly interested in ships and Catalan maritime history.

Carrer de Montcada / Montcada Street↗

Historic street lined with medieval palaces and museums.
Why it matters: Attractive El Born route and part of your tapas-dinner area.

Passeig de Gràcia / Gràcia Boulevard↗

Grand Eixample boulevard known for architecture and upscale shopping.
Why it matters: Main Sunday flex zone for Casa Batlló, La Pedrera and architecture walks.

Casa Batlló / Batlló House↗

Famous Gaudí-designed townhouse with highly sculptural façade and interiors.
Why it matters: Strong Sunday flex choice if you want another major Gaudí experience.

Casa Milà – La Pedrera / Milà House – The Quarry↗

Gaudí apartment building famous for its undulating stone façade and rooftop chimneys.
Why it matters: Alternative Sunday Gaudí experience, especially good for rooftop architecture.

Basílica de la Sagrada Família / Basilica of the Holy Family↗

Gaudí’s monumental basilica and Barcelona’s signature landmark.
Why it matters: Sunday 9:00 AM Mass anchor.

Avinguda de Gaudí / Gaudí Avenue↗

Pedestrian-friendly avenue connecting Sagrada Família and Sant Pau.
Why it matters: Your Sunday walking route and lunch area.

Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau / Saint Paul Art Nouveau Site↗

Former hospital complex designed in the Catalan Modernista style.
Why it matters: Major non-Gaudí example of Barcelona’s Modernista architecture.

Gran Teatre del Liceu / Liceu Grand Theatre↗

Historic Barcelona opera house on La Rambla.
Why it matters: Sunday 5:00 PM Mozart anchor.

Plaça Reial / Royal Square↗

Arcaded historic square just off La Rambla.
Why it matters: Easy Sunday pre-Compline flex option.

Basílica de Santa Maria del Pi / Basilica of Saint Mary of the Pine↗

Large Gothic church known for its rose window.
Why it matters: Optional Sunday evening church stop.

Església de Sant Jaume / Saint James Church↗

Neo-Gothic church on Carrer de Ferran, historically linked to the older Saint James church once located by Saint James Square.
Why it matters: Your planned Sunday 9:00 PM Compline location. The official page currently does not list that service, so it needs date-specific re-verification.

Palau de la Música Catalana / Palace of Catalan Music↗

Spectacular Modernista concert hall filled with stained glass, mosaics and sculpture.
Why it matters: Monday-night concert venue and a major architectural sight itself.

Montserrat / Serrated Mountain↗

Dramatic multi-peaked mountain northwest of Barcelona, named for its saw-toothed profile.
Why it matters: Setting for the monastery, Black Madonna, choir and mountain scenery.

Monestir de Montserrat / Montserrat Monastery↗

Benedictine monastery high on Montserrat mountain.
Why it matters: Core Monday sightseeing destination.

Escolania de Montserrat / Montserrat Boys’ Choir↗

Centuries-old boys’ choir attached to the monastery.
Why it matters: Monday 1:00 PM anchor.

Aeri de Montserrat / Montserrat Aerial Cable Car↗

Yellow aerial cable car from the valley to the monastery area.
Why it matters: Faster and more dramatic mountain-access choice.

Cremallera de Montserrat / Montserrat Rack Railway↗

Mountain railway using a toothed center rail for the steep climb.
Why it matters: More comfortable alternative to the cable car.

Funicular de Sant Joan / Saint John Funicular↗

Funicular railway that climbs higher from the monastery area.
Why it matters: Monday flex option for viewpoints and hiking.

Castell de Santa Florentina / Santa Florentina Castle↗

Medieval-origin castle in Canet de Mar, extensively redesigned during the Modernista era.
Why it matters: Tuesday morning anchor and a very different castle experience from Carcassonne.

Canet de Mar / Canet-by-the-Sea↗

Coastal Catalan town north of Barcelona.
Why it matters: Location of Santa Florentina Castle on your road-trip route.

Cité de Carcassonne / Medieval Walled City of Carcassonne↗

The entire fortified upper city: walls, gates, streets, churches and castle.
Why it matters: Main Tuesday destination; much more than just the Count’s Castle.

Château Comtal / Count’s Castle↗

The fortified castle inside the larger walled Cité.
Why it matters: Main ticketed Carcassonne attraction and the part with the hard winter closing time.

Porte Narbonnaise / Narbonne Gate↗

Major fortified gateway into La Cité.
Why it matters: One of the most recognizable entrances and photo spots.

Basilique Saint-Nazaire / Basilica of Saint Nazarius↗

Historic Romanesque/Gothic church inside La Cité, notable for stained glass.
Why it matters: Important secondary sight after the Count’s Castle.

Bastide Saint-Louis / Saint Louis Lower Town↗

Historic lower town of Carcassonne outside the fortified Cité.
Why it matters: Where you plan to stroll and have dinner Tuesday evening.

Place Carnot / Carnot Square↗

Main square in lower Carcassonne.
Why it matters: Natural center for your lower-town evening walk and dining area.

Rocadest / Rocadest Shopping Center↗

Modern commercial area outside the historic center.
Why it matters: Location of the Jeff de Bruges chocolate stop.

Jeff de Bruges — Carcassonne Rocadest↗

Chocolate shop in the Rocadest shopping area.
Why it matters: Your planned pre-dinner Tuesday shopping stop.
